title: Summary As an avid learner of stock investing, I look to inv
text:
Summary As an avid learner of stock investing, I look to investing greats as role models for investing strategy. One such book that has had a profound influence on my investing approach is "One Up on Wall Street" by Peter Lynch. In this article I apply his teachings to show why three dividend stocks are strong buys.

( "One Up on Wall Street" by Peter Lynch )
Introduction Peter Lynch may not be well known to new investors today, but to those investing since the 1970s, they may know him as the greatest investor not named Warren Buffett. His returns absolutely trounced the market: from 1977 to 1990 the S&P 500 had an annual total return of 13.4%, but Peter Lynch's Fidelity Magellan Fund averaged 29%. The generated alpha was more than the market's total returns:
( Deconstructing Peter Lynch by Daniel Sotiroff )
What was his secret? Peter Lynch is perhaps universally known for saying "buy what you know." Meaning I like iPhones, thus I should buy Apple ( AAPL ), right? Not so fast, actually.
